headline: Approved a $43,468,416 capital loan order, rescinded Hope Ave. special speed limits, and expanded the Burncoat High and Middle Schools project fund.
summary: The council approved a $43,468,416 loan order on an 8-3 vote. It also adopted a request for a report on a possible $100 million street and sidewalk loan program. Many traffic, sidewalk, parking, and zoning petitions were referred to committees or accepted.
decisions: Approved a $43,468,416 capital loan order, 8-3.
Adopted an order asking the City Manager for a report on a possible $20 million per year loan for street and sidewalk work, 7-3.
Approved the transfer of MSBA Stabilization Fund money to the New High School Fund and closure of the MSBA Stabilization Fund, 10-0 (Ojeda recused).
Approved expanding the New High School Fund to include the Burncoat High and Middle Schools project, 10-0 (Ojeda recused).
Voted to advertise four proposed salary ordinance amendments, 10-0 (Toomey absent).
Adopted year-end capital transfers and related grant, transfer, and prior-year payment items, 11-0.
Adopted a resolution to accept and spend a $3,183,690 state preparedness grant, 11-0.
Adopted chairman's orders 11a through 11j, including a request for a draft ordinance to reduce minimum off-street parking requirements.
Adopted an order asking for a neighborhood meeting on noise from St. Joan of Arc Church, and referred the noise ordinance discussion to Public Safety Committee.
Adopted an order asking the Commissioner of Emergency Communications and Management to research 911 follow-up surveys, 9-0 (Bergman, Economou absent).
Voted to rescind the 35 and 30 mph special speed regulations on Hope Ave., 11-0.
Adopted an order asking for a report on streetlights out of operation and repair timelines.
Referred the joint Public Works and Traffic and Parking pavement management review request to both committees.
Adopted, as amended, an order asking for a report on the Town of Holden sewer use lawsuit.
Held an order on Canal District outreach reports under privilege.
Adopted, as amended, an order on the Declaration of Independence statue, adding a refurbished plaque request.
Referred a youth tobacco and vaping meeting request to Public Health and Human Services Committee, 11-0.
Adopted an order asking the Commissioner of Public Works to study tree root damage to sewers, and referred it to Public Works Committee.
Adopted an order asking for a legal opinion on developers at 4 Brandt Ln. using Pine Hill Rd., as amended, 9-0 (Bilotta absent, King abstained).
Adopted an order asking for a plan on conservation land deeding in light of the housing crisis.
Referred an order on youth busking and vending permits to Education Committee.
Held one City Council Office staff vacancy communication under privilege.
Referred City Charter and City Council Office communications to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee.
Referred the Worcester Regional Research Bureau OZ Zones report to Economic Development Committee.
Referred the zoning map petition for 321 Greenwood St. to Economic Development Committee.
Referred the zoning map petition for 455 Grove St. to Economic Development Committee.
Accepted the Economic Development Committee report on NCAA events, 10-1 (King opposed).
Accepted the Economic Development Committee report on NCAA tournament criteria, 9-1 (Bilotta absent, King opposed).
Accepted Public Safety Committee reports on food permitting and police reports.
Accepted and adopted 13 sidewalk and resurfacing petitions, items 19a through 19m.
Accepted and adopted, as amended by Councilor Economou, the Proctor St. guardrail petition.
Accepted committee reports recommending Leave to Withdraw for repaving requests on Vinton St., Gilman Rd., and Norton St.
Referred the Public Works Committee Rd. Burncoat-related sidewalk request, item 19w, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Voted to advertise proposed parking, stop sign, and handicap space ordinances, items 20a through 20m, 10-0 (King abstained).
Accepted and adopted 12 traffic sign, crosswalk, and parking orders, items 20n through 20y.
Accepted the report on the Salisbury St. crosswalk repainting request, placed on file.
Accepted Traffic and Parking Committee reports on Shrewsbury St. crosswalk requests, items 21a through 21z.
Accepted Traffic and Parking Committee reports on Shrewsbury St. crosswalk requests, items 22a through 22h.
Adopted a $43,468,416 loan order for capital improvements.
Ordained 26 traffic, parking, and salary ordinances, items 24a through 24z, 11-0.
Ordained the salary ordinance amendments, items 25a through 25c, 11-0.
Placed on file the Beaver Brook Dog Park audit order.
Held City Council Office survey and staffing communications under privilege a second time, 10-1 (Bilotta opposed).
Took no action on a tabled legal opinion order on rent control.
Adopted an order asking for a report on community policing on Boylston St., 7-3.
Suspended the rules to extend public participation by one hour, 11-0.
Referred the Gordon Davis sump pump request at 10 Varnum St. to the City Manager.
Set public hearings for August 18, 2026 at 6 p.m. on conduit and pole location requests from Charter, National Grid, and Verizon.
Referred speed hump, parking, and bus stop requests, items 9a through 9l, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Referred stone wall, stone deposit, and dam requests, items 7a through 7e, to Department of Public Works.
Referred the 95 Vernon St. Adaptive Reuse Overlay District zoning request to Planning Board.
Referred street resurfacing, sidewalk, and sewer extension requests, items 7g through 7p, to Public Works Committee.
Referred parking, traffic, and signal requests, items 7q through 7z, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Referred crosswalk, parking, and speed hump requests, items 8a through 8z, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Held three City Council confirmation appointments under privilege.
Referred the 128 Providence St. zoning map amendment to Planning Board.
Referred the GreenTech Park Tax Increment Financing Zone resolution to Economic Development Committee.
Held the municipal civilian review board report under privilege.
Referred a Main Street loading zone and parking ordinance to Traffic and Parking Committee.
